after.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,1,0)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
$r=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨1,1,0⟩.$ From the vectorial equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨-2,-3,1⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨-2,-3,1⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,-3,1⟩ & =⟨1,1,0⟩\cdot ⟨-2,-3,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,-3,1⟩ & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-2,-3,1⟩ & =-5 \\ -2x-3y+z & =-5 \\ -2x-3y+z+5 & =0 \\ 2x+3y-z-5 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Given the Cartesian equation 3x+5y+15=0 of the plane Π, find an equation of Π in the form (r−p)⋅n=0.

a
(r−⟨0,3,0⟩)⋅⟨3,5,−1⟩=0
b
(r−⟨0,−3,0⟩)⋅⟨3,5,0⟩=0
c
(r−⟨0,−3,1⟩)⋅⟨3,0,5⟩=0
d
(r−⟨0,0,−3⟩)⋅⟨5,3,0⟩=0
e
(r−⟨0,0,3⟩)⋅⟨5,3,0⟩=0
Submit

decision.explanation: The coefficients give the normal vector ⟨3,5,0⟩. The point (0,-3,0) lies on the plane since 3(0)+5(-3)+15=0. Thus option b expands to the given Cartesian equation.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $3x+5y+15=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
after.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨3,5,0⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+5y+15 & =0 \\ 5y & =-3x-15 \\ y & =-\frac{3}{5}x-3.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$, we get $y=-3.$ Hence, the point $P(0,-3,0)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,-3,0⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,-3,0⟩)\cdot ⟨3,5,0⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Plane Given Its Cartesian Equation
content.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $3x+5y+15=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
content.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨3,5,0⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+5y+15 & =0 \\ 5y & =-3x-15 \\ y & =-\frac{3}{5}x-3.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$, we get $y=-3.$ Hence, the point $P(0,-3,0)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,-3,0⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,-3,0⟩)\cdot ⟨3,5,0⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $5y-z+17=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
after.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨0,5,-1⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}5y-z+17 & =0 \\ z & =5y+17.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $y=0$, we get $z=17.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,17)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,17⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,17⟩)\cdot ⟨0,5,-1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $5y-z+17=0$ of the plane $Π$, find an equation of $Π$ in the form $(r-p)\cdot n=0.$
content.worked_solution:
First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨0,5,-1⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}5y-z+17 & =0 \\ z & =5y+17.\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $y=0$, we get $z=17.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,17)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,17⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,17⟩)\cdot ⟨0,5,-1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(0,2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the line 

$$
\frac{y-3}{-5}=\frac{z}{4},\,x=1
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,2,3⟩.$ From the Cartesian equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨0,-5,4⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨0,-5,4⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,-5,4⟩ & =⟨0,2,3⟩\cdot ⟨0,-5,4⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,-5,4⟩ & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,-5,4⟩ & =2 \\ -5y+4z & =2 \\ -5y+4z-2 & =0 \\ 5y-4z+2 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(0,2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the line 

$$
\frac{y-3}{-5}=\frac{z}{4},\,x=1
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,2,3⟩.$ From the Cartesian equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨0,-5,4⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨0,-5,4⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨0,-5,4⟩ & =⟨0,2,3⟩\cdot ⟨0,-5,4⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨0,-5,4⟩ & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨0,-5,4⟩ & =2 \\ -5y+4z & =2 \\ -5y+4z-2 & =0 \\ 5y-4z+2 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨5,0,3⟩-⟨2,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨3,2,2⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨1,1,-1⟩-⟨2,-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,3,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now,  we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-10i+4j+11k \\  & =⟨-10,4,11⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-10,4,11⟩ & =⟨5,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨-10,4,11⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-10,4,11⟩ & =-17\end{aligned}
